caption: Newanforbi v. Derrick et al.
claims: 42 USC 1983: 1A Retaliation, 14A Equal Protection, Due Process
status: CASE CLOSED — E.D. Cal. No. 2:26-cv-00004-DJC-JDP terminated (confirmed Aug. 26, 2026). Derrick/Noguchi dismissed Jul. 22 under Rule 41(a)(1)(A)(i); Palacios dismissed Aug. 20–21 under Rule 41(a)(1)(A)(i) in response to Mag. Peterson's Aug. 13 OSC (ECF No. 33); OSC discharged and docket closed. No further action.
judge: Hon. Daniel J. Calabretta / Mag. Peterson
note: Palacios's MTD GRANTED Jul. 24; FAC dismissed w/ leave to amend by Aug. 7. Jul. 22 dismissal of Derrick/Noguchi was valid as a matter of right (no answer/MSJ served). Aug. 20, 2026 Notice of Voluntary Dismissal of Katie Palacios filed (Rule 41(a)(1)(A)(i)). CASE CLOSED Aug. 26, 2026 — OSC discharged; E.D. Cal. docket terminated.
defendants: Andrew Derrick (#6910) — Notice of Voluntary Dismissal filed Jul. 22, 2026 (self-executing under Rule 41(a)(1)(A)(i)); Jul. 24, 2026 order nonetheless treats him as the sole remaining defendant if no amended complaint is filed — tension unresolved on the docket; Katie Palacios — MTD GRANTED Jul. 24, 2026 (failed all four state-actor tests); claims DISMISSED WITH LEAVE TO AMEND; then Notice of Voluntary Dismissal filed Aug. 20, 2026 under Rule 41(a)(1)(A)(i); Gary Noguchi (#7284) — Notice of Voluntary Dismissal filed Jul. 22, 2026 (self-executing); Jul. 24, 2026 order separately dismissed claims against him for failure to allege supervisory liability
causes: Substantive Due Process — Arbitrary Abuse of Power
key_facts: Derrick told Plaintiff at their first meeting (Jan. 2025): 'You do not have freedom of speech. Not in HOPE group you don't.' — preceded by: 'it would not be good for you if you didn't stop.' Plaintiff had been in HOPE group ~5 years despite completing all homework multiple times; group repeatedly reset due to clinician turnover. Derrick and Palacios jointly revoked the standard 10-minute grace period (Apr. 2025), stating: 'You are clearly abusing the 10-minute as an excuse to show up late.' FedEx job (Mar. 2025, $20/hr): Plaintiff was denied a scheduling accommodation and forced to resign (~Apr. 17, 2025); lost wages ≥ $1,500; ongoing ~$600/week. CTM (mid-2025): Palacios labeled Plaintiff 'ringleader' whose speech encouraged others; Derrick gave a negative oral report focused on Plaintiff's speech; Noguchi denied reassignment on the spot despite actual knowledge of the retaliatory conflict. Chilling effect documented: Plaintiff abandoned a Form 22 reassignment request when Derrick appeared and said 'You're just finding something to complain about, huh?' — Plaintiff stuttered and could not speak. Nov. 2025 Discharge Review incorporated 'disruptive'/'ringleader' characterizations; Noguchi reviewed and approved. Comparator A (white male, same HOPE program/agent): received 1–2 min home visits, casino trip approved, Derrick personally helped file grievances — no threats or escalation. Comparator B (Black male, supervised by Derrick): Derrick stated certain offenders 'should be lined up and shot'; cited out of bounds at family park gatherings → arrest and custody. Both comparators provided sworn declarations under 28 U.S.C. § 1746.
procedural_status: FAC filed Jan. 12, 2026. Service/MTD briefing through spring 2026 (Docs 9, 14, 24) culminated in Mag. Peterson's July 24 order: Palacios fails all four Ninth Circuit state-actor tests (Rawson misquote flagged with Rule 11(b)(2) reminder); Derrick/Noguchi MTQ denied as moot, MTD granted on 1A/due-process grounds; FAC dismissed with leave to amend by Aug. 7, 2026. Plaintiff had already filed a July 22 Notice of Voluntary Dismissal Without Prejudice as to Derrick and Noguchi under Rule 41(a)(1)(A)(i) — self-executing at filing, and not referenced in the July 24 order. SLB rejected an $85,000 global demand May 23, 2026. Aug. 13, 2026 OSC (ECF No. 33) ordered Plaintiff to show cause within 14 days (by Aug. 27) why the case should not be dismissed for failure to amend, or to file an amended complaint; also directed the Clerk to terminate Derrick and Noguchi per the July 22 notice. Plaintiff's Aug. 20–21 Palacios dismissal was the response electing not to continue. CASE CLOSED (confirmed Aug. 26, 2026): OSC discharged; E.D. Cal. docket terminated — no further deadlines.
risk: Qualified immunity; rebutted by explicit on-record speech-suppression statement, documented race-based comparator disparity, and sworn third-party declarations.
evidence: HOPE Group Session Camera Recordings (Stockton facility)
FedEx Records (job offer, training schedule, forced resignation ~Apr. 17, 2025)
Comparator A Sworn Declaration (28 U.S.C. § 1746) — white parolee, casino trip, Form 602 assistance
Comparator B Sworn Declaration (28 U.S.C. § 1746) — Black parolee, 'shot' remarks, park arrest

July 2, 2026 inter-county transfer (Stockton to Santa Clara), one day after Matter 15 state filing naming Noguchi — temporal proximity plus departure from Form 1502-DR's own record of 4 prior comparable violations resolved without transfer
